prompt:
Score each onboarding change. Sub-scores:
- impact 0-3: how many users the targeted step loses and how much this could recover
- evidence 0-3: whether the funnel and the support mail both point at this problem
- confidence 0-2: how likely this kind of change works, judged from the lessons below
- cost 0-2: 2 = config only, 0 = needs new screens and a release
Also give predicted_lift: expected relative change in the target step's conversion, e.g. 0.05.

Lessons from earlier weeks:
Adding new screens (new_screen) was helpful, winning 3 tests (+15.4%, +6.4%, +11.4%), though 1 hurt performance (-7.7%) and 3 showed no clear effect.
Waiting screen info updates (wait_info) were helpful, winning 3 tests (+5.0%, +5.7%, +4.1%), though 1 hurt performance (-6.0%) and 4 showed no clear effect.
Layout changes (layout) were helpful, winning 1 test (+7.0%), while 1 test showed no clear effect.
Redesigns (redesign) and reordering steps (reorder) hurt performance in 1 test each (-7.5% and -3.8% respectively) and showed no clear effect in all other tests.
Copy changes, hints, notifications, and new flows showed no clear effect across all tests.
Predictions underestimated large wins (e.g., predicting +3.0% vs +15.4% measured, +7.0% vs +11.4% measured) and overestimated changes that showed no clear effect or lost.

Changes:
0: [choose_path, new_screen] Companion Visual Style Showcase Screen: Adds a new visual showcase screen before choose_path highlighting different companion art styles and animations. (why: The choose_path step has a median time of 8s but a mean time of 514s, indicating hesitation. Adding visual preview screens previously yielded up to +15.4% conversion wins.)
1: [home, new_screen] Desktop Environment Readiness Screen: Adds a new screen during home setup that checks display overlay access and screen permissions before desktop spawn. (why: Support receives multiple tickets (3 emails) about pets not displaying on desktop or app failing to open, causing drop-offs prior to finish.)
2: [finish, new_screen] Companion Hotkey Activation Screen: Adds a dedicated screen introducing keyboard shortcuts for summoning, hiding, and interacting with the desktop companion. (why: Support receives emails after onboarding regarding confusion on how to control or hide the pet (3 emails), and finish step conversion is only 70.9%.)
3: [adoption, new_screen] Pet Companion Animation Speed Screen: Adds a step during adoption allowing users to select how fast and active their pet moves around the desktop screen. (why: Adding interactive customization screens during adoption previously yielded major conversion gains (+15.4% and +11.4%).)
4: [home, wait_info] Desktop Rendering Progress Status in Waiting: Displays live status updates and an interactive progress indicator while the desktop pet renderer initializes. (why: Waiting screen info changes have consistently won past tests (+5.0%, +5.7%, +4.1%), directly addressing long rendering delays (home mean time of 2336s).)
5: [home, wait_info] Right-Click Interaction Tip Carousel on Waiting: Adds a tip carousel on the waiting screen explaining how to access right-click context menus once the pet spawns. (why: Wait screen updates reduce bounce during long waiting periods and clarify post-onboarding pet control confusion noted in support mail.)
6: [choose_path, layout] Two Column Layout for Path Options: Reconfigures the choose_path screen layout into a clear side-by-side two-column comparison card structure. (why: Layout changes won +7.0% in past tests; side-by-side presentation simplifies decision-making on path selection.)
7: [sign_in, layout] Centered Focus Layout for Sign In Options: Restructures the sign-in screen into a clean centered layout emphasizing account save benefits. (why: 8 support emails complained about missing or reset pets after signing back in, indicating sign-in UX needs clearer framing.)
8: [finish, redesign] Spotlight Layout Redesign of Home Intro Screen: Redesigns home_intro using a spotlight layout with a prominent mascot animation announcing the pet's arrival on the desktop. (why: The final step drop-off is high (overall completion is 27.4%), and finish step mean time is 5815s. A clear call to action on screen completion drives immediate engagement.)
